items.markdown:
Thailand offers several long-term visa options, with the most popular being the `Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa, the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), and standard Non-Immigrant Retirement or Marriage visas`.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B35no1yygRQ&t=247)[[2]](https://traveldudes.com/how-to-settle-as-an-expat-in-thailand/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dhn5Pn97zeE&t=121)[[4]](https://ananpropertygroup.com/understanding-thai-visas-for-long-term-living-and-property/)

Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa

- **Duration:** 10 years (split into two 5-year blocks).[](https://www.hlbthai.com/thailand-long-term-resident-ltr-visa/) [[1]](https://www.hlbthai.com/thailand-long-term-resident-ltr-visa/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QemGMHaYobE)[[3]](https://london.thaiembassy.org/en/page/long-term-resident-visa)[[4]](https://silklegal.com/staying-in-thailand-just-got-a-bit-easier-with-ltr-visas/)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4aULS5TC6QY&t=45)
- **Cost:** 50,000 Baht (approx. $1,500 USD).[](https://www.hlbthai.com/thailand-long-term-resident-ltr-visa/) 
- **Target Groups:** Wealthy global citizens ($1M+ assets), wealthy pensioners (aged 50+ with $80k/year income or $40k with Thai investments), remote workers for large overseas firms, and highly skilled professionals.[](https://www.hlbthai.com/thailand-long-term-resident-ltr-visa/) [[1]](https://kpmg.com/xx/en/our-insights/gms-flash-alert/flash-alert-2025-040.html)
- **Perks:** Tax exemptions on foreign-sourced income for most categories, a 17% flat tax for high-skilled experts, and 1-year reporting instead of 90-day reporting.[](https://www.hlbthai.com/thailand-long-term-resident-ltr-visa/) 

Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)

- **Duration:** 5 years total, allowing stays up to 180 days per entry (extendable once per stay).
- **Target Groups:** Digital nomads, freelancers, and people taking soft power courses (such as Muay Thai, cooking, or medical retreats).
- **Requirements:** 500,000 Baht in savings and proof of remote employment or class enrollment; no minimum annual salary is required.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4aULS5TC6QY&t=45) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4aULS5TC6QY&t=45)

Traditional Non-Immigrant Visas (e.g., Retirement "O" or "O-A")

- **Duration:** 1 year, renewable annually inside Thailand.
- **Target Groups:** Retirees aged 50 and older.
- **Requirements:** Must hold 800,000 Baht in a Thai bank account or show a monthly income/pension of at least 65,000 Baht.[[1]](https://www.siam-legal.com/thailand-visa/1-Year-Thailand-Visa.php)[[2]](https://london.thaiembassy.org/en/publicservice/84508-non-immigrant-visas)[[3]](https://sites.google.com/panyaden.ac.th/parents-and-students/general-information/visas)[[4]](https://www.legalink.net/en/publications/newsletters/changed-rules-for-ltr-long-term-resident-visas-in-thailand/6210/)

If you'd like to narrow down the best choice, please tell me:

- **Your purpose** (retirement, remote work, investing, or studying)
- **Your age** 
- **Your estimated yearly income or savings** 

I can help identify the exact visa category that fits your situation.
